name: Temporal Knowledge
summary: Represent knowledge as sourced assertions with transaction time, validity intervals, supersession, and policy weights.
purpose: Prevent a knowledge base from flattening changing claims into timeless truth by preserving when an assertion was recorded, when it applies, what supersedes it, and how its influence was calculated.
use_when: Facts change over time or have bounded validity periods.
Multiple sources assert different values for the same entity and attribute.
An agent must answer current-state, history, or as-of questions.
avoid_when: A policy weight would be misrepresented as an objective probability of truth.
The domain requires a formally validated temporal or probabilistic model not supplied here.

procedure.operation: Store each assertion as an append-only entity-attribute-value event with source and transaction time.
Store valid-from and valid-until separately from the time the system recorded the assertion.
Represent retraction and corroboration as new events rather than destructive updates to history.
Treat a different value for the same entity and attribute as an explicit conflict candidate, not automatic semantic contradiction.
Resolve current or as-of views from ordered events and declared validity boundaries.
Expose source trust, decay, corroboration, and anomaly thresholds as inspectable policy parameters.

invariants: Transaction time and valid time remain distinct.
History is append-only and prior assertions remain inspectable.
Weights and lifecycle labels are explicitly identified as policy heuristics.

failure_modes.mode: A different string value is treated as a semantic contradiction without normalization or domain logic.
failure_modes.mitigation: Label it a conflict candidate and apply domain-specific equivalence or contradiction rules separately.

failure_modes.mode: Recency or repeated assertion is interpreted as truth.
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep source quality, corroboration independence, evidence, and policy weight as separate fields.

provenance.title: Nexus Gravitas
provenance.qualification: The contract generalizes the implementation while explicitly labeling its weighting constants and anomaly thresholds as policy.

provenance.title: Gravitas weighting implementation
provenance.qualification: Corroboration, contradiction, floor, ceiling, and decay values are implementation constants, not calibrated probabilities.

limitations: Entity resolution, semantic normalization, and independent-source detection are outside this contract.
Temporal correctness depends on trustworthy clocks and correctly modeled validity intervals.
Policy weights require domain evaluation before consequential use.
